messages:
maria: Heads up — rolling BIOS+BMC push in eu-central (euc1) hit a small subset of racks. ~5% of nodes booted to emergency shell after reboot. Secure boot variable shows as toggled to 'disabled' on a few machines. Can infra eyeball provisioning?

deploy-bot: Deploy started by infra-team at 09:12 UTC — firmware-batch-2026-03-20.

sam: On it. Pulling logs from an affected host:
```
Apr 20 09:13:45 kernel: efivar: failed to update variable: I/O error
Apr 20 09:13:45 systemd: Started Emergency Shell.
Apr 20 09:13:46 ipmi: BMC keystore update failed: write error 0x5
```

jordan: Interesting — are we seeing signature verification failures on kernel/bootloader? or NVRAM write issues?

maria: Not seeing signature failures. Signed image checks out. Most traces point to efivar/NVRAM writes and BMC keystore rotation errors.

lee: Can we map affected hosts to BMC/BIOs versions? Could be a regression in the BMC write path.

sam: Quick grep: all affected hosts are on BMC 2.14.0-rc3 and BIOS 1.23.4. Non-affected racks are on BMC 2.13.8 + BIOS 1.23.2. Also noticed the affected racks share the same OOB switch firmware (oob-sw-5.6.1).

pavel: Marked the eu-central GPU pool as draining for new long jobs to avoid cascading evictions while we triage.

maria: FYI — draining will reduce available GPU capacity ~12% during peak. If we hold this for the next 6h we'll likely see customer throttles and some SLA tickets. Need quick mitigation plan.

jordan: Proposal: rollback BMC on a canary rack to 2.13.8, test full reboot + secure var persistence, then roll in 10% batches. Meanwhile, add a manual runbook to clear efivars via serial on nodes stuck in emergency shell.

lee: I can run the canary rollback now. Pushing downgrade image to canary BMCs. Will report back in ~8–10m.

sam: Also consider a software mitigation: when keystore rotation is in-progress, block writes to efivar by remounting efivarfs read-only until rotation completes. Might prevent corruption during failed writes (low-confidence, needs testing).

maria: For immediate traffic mitigation, enable routing fallback for scheduled heavy jobs to us-west for jobs >4h to prevent SLA breaches. Ops: update routing policy.

lee: Canary rollback complete. Rebooted 6 nodes in rack-a. All 6 booted to normal OS with secure boot state preserved. Provisioning tests OK. :thumbsup:

maria: Excellent. Start phased rollback across affected racks with 10% batches, watch for efivar write errors and BMC keystore logs. Coordinate with on-call for each batch.

pavel: Rollout plan noted. Cost heads-up: inter-region fallback and additional failed retries could add ~$8k/day if we keep cross-region routing and draining active. Flagging finance/alerts.

jordan: I'll add a short runbook here for manual efivar reset via serial if we encounter stuck nodes: 
```
1) Connect to serial console via oob-jumphost
2) mount -t efivarfs efivarfs /sys/firmware/efi/efivars
3) for var in $(grep -l "Corrupt" /sys/firmware/efi/efivars/*); do printf "Removing $var"; rm "$var"; done
4) reboot
```

maria: Thanks. After 2 batches succeed, we'll re-enable normal routing and stop draining. Keep me posted every 15m during rollout.

deploy-bot: Rolling downgrade job queued: rollback-bmc-2026-03-20 (10% batch size, automated pause after each batch).

lee: Batch 1 done — no regressions. Starting 10m wait then batch 2.

sam: Monitoring logs and provisioning metrics. No new emergency shells in batch 1.

maria: Good. If any node still shows efivar errors, tag me and we'll escalate to firmware vendor.

pavel: Noted. I'll also open a cost-impact ticket for finance with the interim estimate and keep it updated.

lee: batch 2 complete, batch 3 in progress.

maria: Thanks team — keep communications here. We'll close thread when all racks are confirmed stable. :white_check_mark:
